subject: phase3_controller_verification_handoff
statement: Implement provider-free controller-owned verification recovery and deterministic candidate test separation before any further Phase 3 scored execution.
selected_option: preserve the 12/16 cost boundary, recover only explicitly deferred scope-valid patches through mandatory controller verification, and freeze production-with-supplemental-tests candidate publication for new protocols

alternatives.option: increase the common hard tool limit
alternatives.rejected_reason: A larger undifferentiated limit does not guarantee final verification and weakens the measured containment boundary.

alternatives.option: accept every failed result that contains a patch
alternatives.rejected_reason: Worker failure can represent semantic, permission, environment, or implementation errors and cannot be converted into acceptance without an explicit narrow handoff plus controller verification.

alternatives.option: remove candidate test hunks only after an evaluator conflict
alternatives.rejected_reason: Post-hoc mutation depends on hidden evaluator outcomes and invalidates the frozen experiment contract.

rationale: The Requests direct worker already supplied a complete patch artifact and a structured focused verification command, while the scheduler already owns isolated integration verification and rollback. A narrow verification-deferred state connects those existing mechanisms without adding model calls. The full-mode conflict also shows that complete implementation authority and scored benchmark submission need separate immutable identities. Freezing public test-path classification before execution preserves all worker output and prevents evaluator outcomes from deciding which hunks are scored.
expected_outcome: A bounded worker can hand a completed patch to deterministic runtime verification without falsely claiming worker-side tests, while new Phase 3 runs retain candidate-authored tests without allowing hidden evaluator conflicts or post-hoc edits to define the scored production patch.
acceptance_refs: focused candidate publication and evaluator selection tests
